The aggregate of material form has no object. The other four aggregates have objects. The aggregate of consciousness is mind. The other four aggregates are not mind. Three aggregates are mental factors. Two aggregates are not mental factors. Three aggregates are joined with mind. The aggregate of material form is dissociated from mind. The aggregate of consciousness cannot be described as "joined with mind" or as "dissociated from mind". Three aggregates are mingled with mind. The aggregate of material form is not mingled with mind. The aggregate of consciousness cannot be described as "mingled with mind" or as "not mingled with mind". Three aggregates are produced by mind. The aggregate of consciousness is not produced by mind. The aggregate of material form may be produced by mind or not. Three aggregates arise together with mind. The aggregate of consciousness does not arise together with mind. The aggregate of material form may arise together with mind or not. Three aggregates follow along with mind. The aggregate of consciousness does not follow along with mind. The aggregate of material form may follow along with mind or not. Three aggregates are mingled with mind and produced by it. Two aggregates are not mingled with mind and produced by it. Three aggregates are mingled with mind, produced by it, and arise together with it. Two aggregates are not. Three aggregates are mingled with mind, produced by it, and follow along with it. Two aggregates are not.

The aggregate of consciousness is internal. Three aggregates are external. The aggregate of material form may be internal or external. Four aggregates are not derived. The aggregate of material form may be derived or not derived, may be taken up at birth or not taken up. Four aggregates are not clinging. The aggregate of mental formations may be clinging or not. The aggregate of material form can be clung to. The other four aggregates may be able to be clung to or not. The aggregate of material form is dissociated from clinging. The other four aggregates may be joined with clinging or dissociated from it. The aggregate of material form cannot be described as "clinging that can be clung to"; it can be clung to without being clinging. Three aggregates cannot be described as "clinging that can be clung to"; they may be able to be clung to without being clinging, or may not be describable as such. The aggregate of mental formations may be clinging that can be clung to, may be able to be clung to without being clinging, or may not be describable as either. The aggregate of material form cannot be described as "clinging joined with clinging" or as "joined with clinging without being clinging". Three aggregates cannot be described as "clinging joined with clinging"; they may be joined with clinging without being clinging, or may not be describable as such. The aggregate of mental formations may be clinging joined with clinging, may be joined with clinging without being clinging, or may not be describable as either. The aggregate of material form is dissociated from clinging yet able to be clung to. The other four aggregates may be dissociated from clinging yet able to be clung to, dissociated from it and unable to be clung to, or not describable as either.

Four aggregates are not defilements. The aggregate of mental formations may be a defilement or not. The aggregate of material form is open to defilement. The other four aggregates may be open to defilement or not. The aggregate of material form is undefiled. The other four aggregates may be defiled or undefiled. The aggregate of material form is dissociated from the defilements. The other four aggregates may be joined with the defilements or dissociated from them. The aggregate of material form cannot be described as "a defilement open to defilement"; it is open to defilement without being a defilement. Three aggregates cannot be described as "defilements open to defilement"; they may be open to defilement without being defilements, or may not be describable as such. The aggregate of mental formations may be a defilement open to defilement, may be open to defilement without being a defilement, or may not be describable as either. The aggregate of material form cannot be described as "a defilement that is defiled" or as "defiled without being a defilement". Three aggregates cannot be described as "defilements that are defiled"; they may be defiled without being defilements, or may not be describable as such. The aggregate of mental formations may be a defilement that is defiled, may be defiled without being a defilement, or may not be describable as either.

The aggregate of material form cannot be described as "a defilement joined with the defilements" or as "joined with the defilements without being a defilement". Three aggregates cannot be described as "defilements joined with the defilements"; they may be joined with the defilements without being defilements, or may not be describable as such. The aggregate of mental formations may be a defilement joined with the defilements, may be joined with the defilements without being a defilement, or may not be describable as either. The aggregate of material form is dissociated from the defilements yet open to defilement. The other four aggregates may be dissociated from the defilements yet open to defilement, dissociated from them and not open to defilement, or not describable as either.

The aggregate of material form is not to be abandoned by seeing. The other four aggregates may be abandoned by seeing or not. The aggregate of material form is not to be abandoned by meditative development. The other four aggregates may be abandoned by development or not. The aggregate of material form does not have root causes to be abandoned by seeing. The other four aggregates may have root causes to be abandoned by seeing or not. The aggregate of material form does not have root causes to be abandoned by development. The other four aggregates may have root causes to be abandoned by development or not. The aggregate of material form is without thought. The other four aggregates may have thought or not. The aggregate of material form is without examination. The other four aggregates may have examination or not. The aggregate of material form is without joy. The other four aggregates may have joy or not. The aggregate of material form is not accompanied by joy. The other four aggregates may be accompanied by joy or not. Two aggregates are not accompanied by happiness. Three aggregates may be accompanied by happiness or not. Two aggregates are not accompanied by equanimity. Three aggregates may be accompanied by equanimity or not.

The aggregate of material form belongs to the sense sphere. The other four aggregates may belong to the sense sphere or not. The aggregate of material form does not belong to the fine-material sphere. The other four aggregates may belong to the fine-material sphere or not. The aggregate of material form does not belong to the immaterial sphere. The other four aggregates may belong to the immaterial sphere or not. The aggregate of material form is included in the round of existence. The other four aggregates may be included in the round of existence or outside it. The aggregate of material form does not lead out of the round. The other four aggregates may lead out of the round or not. The aggregate of material form is not fixed in its outcome. The other four aggregates may be fixed or not fixed. The aggregate of material form can be surpassed. The other four aggregates may be surpassable or unsurpassable. The aggregate of material form is free from conflict. The other four aggregates may involve conflict or be free from conflict.
The Section of Questions and Answers is finished.
The Analysis of the Aggregates is finished.
2. Analysis of the Sense-Fields
1. Classification According to the Discourses

There are twelve sense-fields – the eye sense-field, the sense-field of sights, the ear sense-field, the sense-field of sounds, the nose sense-field, the sense-field of smells, the tongue sense-field, the sense-field of tastes, the body sense-field, the sense-field of things touched, the mind sense-field, and the sense-field of mental objects. ⤵ The eye is impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. Sights are impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. The ear is impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. Sounds are impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. The nose is impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. Smells are impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. The tongue is impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. Tastes are impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. The body is impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. Things touched are impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. The mind is impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change. Mental objects are impermanent, unsatisfactory, not a self, and subject to change.
The Classification According to the Discourses is finished.
2. Classification According to the Abhidhamma

There are twelve sense-fields – the eye sense-field, the ear sense-field, the nose sense-field, the tongue sense-field, the body sense-field, the mind sense-field, the sense-field of sights, the sense-field of sounds, the sense-field of smells, the sense-field of tastes, the sense-field of things touched, and the sense-field of mental objects.

Therein, what is the eye sense-field? The eye that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements, included in one's own body, invisible, and offering resistance; the eye – itself invisible and offering resistance – by which one has seen, sees, will see, or may see a sight that is visible and offers resistance: this is the eye, this is the eye sense-field, this is the eye element, this is the eye faculty; this is a world, this is a door, this is an ocean; this is the bright surface, this is a field, this is a base; this is a guide, this is an eye; this is the near shore, this is an empty village. This is called "the eye sense-field".

Therein, what is the ear sense-field? The ear that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements, included in one's own body, invisible, and offering resistance; the ear – itself invisible and offering resistance – by which one has heard, hears, will hear, or may hear a sound that is invisible and offers resistance: this is the ear, this is the ear sense-field, this is the ear element, this is the ear faculty; this is a world, this is a door, this is an ocean; this is the bright surface, this is a field, this is a base; this is the near shore, this is an empty village. This is called "the ear sense-field".

Therein, what is the nose sense-field? The nose that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements, included in one's own body, invisible, and offering resistance; the nose – itself invisible and offering resistance – by which one has smelled, smells, will smell, or may smell a smell that is invisible and offers resistance: this is the nose, this is the nose sense-field, this is the nose element, this is the nose faculty; this is a world, this is a door, this is an ocean; this is the bright surface, this is a field, this is a base; this is the near shore, this is an empty village. This is called "the nose sense-field".

Therein, what is the tongue sense-field? The tongue that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements, included in one's own body, invisible, and offering resistance; the tongue – itself invisible and offering resistance – by which one has tasted, tastes, will taste, or may taste a taste that is invisible and offers resistance: this is the tongue, this is the tongue sense-field, this is the tongue element, this is the tongue faculty; this is a world, this is a door, this is an ocean; this is the bright surface, this is a field, this is a base; this is the near shore, this is an empty village. This is called "the tongue sense-field".

Therein, what is the body sense-field? The body that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements, included in one's own body, invisible, and offering resistance; the body – itself invisible and offering resistance – by which one has touched, touches, will touch, or may touch something touchable that is invisible and offers resistance: this is the body, this is the body sense-field, this is the body element, this is the body faculty; this is a world, this is a door, this is an ocean; this is the bright surface, this is a field, this is a base; this is the near shore, this is an empty village. This is called "the body sense-field".

Therein, what is the mind sense-field? As a single class, the mind sense-field is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is mind with a root cause, and mind without a root cause. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is wholesome mind, unwholesome mind, and neutral mind. ⤵ As a fourfold class: there is mind belonging to the sense sphere, to the fine-material sphere, to the immaterial sphere, and mind not included in any sphere. ⤵ As a fivefold class: there is mind joined with the faculty of pleasure, joined with the faculty of pain, joined with the faculty of gladness, joined with the faculty of sadness, and joined with the faculty of equanimity. ⤵ As a sixfold class: there is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, and mind-consciousness. This is the mind sense-field as a sixfold class. ⤵ As a sevenfold class: there is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, the mind element, and the mind-consciousness element. This is the mind sense-field as a sevenfold class. ⤵ As an eightfold class: there is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness – which may be accompanied by pleasure or by pain – the mind element, and the mind-consciousness element. This is the mind sense-field as an eightfold class. ⤵ As a ninefold class: there is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, the mind element, and the mind-consciousness element – which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is the mind sense-field as a ninefold class. ⤵ As a tenfold class: there is eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness – which may be accompanied by pleasure or by pain – the mind element, and the mind-consciousness element – which may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. This is the mind sense-field as a tenfold class. ⤵ As a single class, the mind sense-field is this: it is joined with contact. ⤵ As a twofold class: there is mind with a root cause, and mind without a root cause. ⤵ As a threefold class: there is mind joined with pleasant feeling, mind joined with painful feeling, and mind joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant… Thus the mind sense-field is classified in many ways. This is called "the mind sense-field".

Therein, what is the sense-field of sights? The sight that is the shining of colour derived from the four great elements, visible and offering resistance – blue, yellow, red, white, black, crimson, leaf-green, greenish, the colour of a mango shoot; long, short, small, large, round, circular, square, six-sided, eight-sided, sixteen-sided; low, high; shade and sunshine; light and darkness; cloud, mist, smoke, and dust; the shining colour of the moon's disc, the shining colour of the sun's disc, the shining colour of the stars, the shining colour of a mirror's disc, the shining colour of gems, conch shells, pearls, and cat's-eye, the shining colour of gold and silver; or whatever other sight there is, derived from the four great elements, the shining of colour, visible and offering resistance; the sight – visible and offering resistance – which one has seen, sees, will see, or may see with the eye that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a sight, this is the sense-field of sights, this is the element of sights. This is called "the sense-field of sights".

Therein, what is the sense-field of sounds? The sound that is derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance – the sound of drums, the sound of small drums, the sound of conches, the sound of tom-toms, the sound of singing, the sound of instruments, the sound of cymbals, the sound of clapping hands, the cries of living beings, the sound of elements colliding, the sound of wind, the sound of water, the sound of humans, the sound of non-humans; or whatever other sound there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance; the sound – invisible and offering resistance – which one has heard, hears, will hear, or may hear with the ear that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a sound, this is the sense-field of sounds, this is the element of sounds. This is called "the sense-field of sounds".

Therein, what is the sense-field of smells? The smell that is derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance – the smell of roots, the smell of heartwood, the smell of bark, the smell of leaves, the smell of flowers, the smell of fruits, raw smells, putrid smells, pleasant smells, unpleasant smells; or whatever other smell there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance; the smell – invisible and offering resistance – which one has smelled, smells, will smell, or may smell with the nose that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a smell, this is the sense-field of smells, this is the element of smells. This is called "the sense-field of smells".

Therein, what is the sense-field of tastes? The taste that is derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance – the taste of roots, the taste of stems, the taste of bark, the taste of leaves, the taste of flowers, the taste of fruits; sour, sweet, bitter, pungent, salty, alkaline, acrid, astringent; tasty, unappetising; or whatever other taste there is, derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance; the taste – invisible and offering resistance – which one has tasted, tastes, will taste, or may taste with the tongue that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a taste, this is the sense-field of tastes, this is the element of tastes. This is called "the sense-field of tastes".

Therein, what is the sense-field of things touched? The earth element, the fire element, the air element; hard, soft, smooth, rough; pleasant to the touch, painful to the touch; heavy, light; the touchable thing – invisible and offering resistance – which one has touched, touches, will touch, or may touch with the body that is invisible and offers resistance: this is a touchable thing, this is the sense-field of things touched, this is the element of things touched. This is called "the sense-field of things touched".

Therein, what is the sense-field of mental objects? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the material form that is invisible and offers no resistance and is included in the sense-field of mental objects, and the unconditioned element. ⤵ Therein, what is the aggregate of feeling? As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is joined with contact. As a twofold class: there is feeling with a root cause, and feeling without one. As a threefold class: there is wholesome feeling, unwholesome feeling, and neutral feeling… thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways… thus the aggregate of feeling is classified in many ways. This is called "the aggregate of feeling". ⤵ Therein, what is the aggregate of perception? As a single class, the aggregate of perception is joined with contact. As a twofold class: there is perception with a root cause, and perception without one. As a threefold class: there is wholesome perception, unwholesome perception, and neutral perception… thus the aggregate of perception is classified up to ten ways… thus the aggregate of perception is classified in many ways. This is called "the aggregate of perception". ⤵ Therein, what is the aggregate of mental formations? As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is joined with mind. As a twofold class: there are formations that are root causes, and formations that are not. As a threefold class: there are wholesome formations, unwholesome formations, and neutral formations… thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways… thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified in many ways. This is called "the aggregate of mental formations". ⤵ Therein, what is the material form that is invisible, offers no resistance, and is included in the sense-field of mental objects? The faculty of femininity, the faculty of masculinity… physical food. This is called the material form that is "invisible, offers no resistance, and is included in the sense-field of mental objects". ⤵ Therein, what is the unconditioned element? The ending of desire, the ending of hatred, and the ending of delusion – this is called "the unconditioned element".
This is called the sense-field of mental objects.
The Classification According to the Abhidhamma is finished.
3. The Section of Questions and Answers

There are twelve sense-fields – the eye sense-field, the sense-field of sights, the ear sense-field, the sense-field of sounds, the nose sense-field, the sense-field of smells, the tongue sense-field, the sense-field of tastes, the body sense-field, the sense-field of things touched, the mind sense-field, and the sense-field of mental objects.
Of the twelve sense-fields, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral… how many involve conflict, how many are free from conflict?
1. The Triads

Ten sense-fields are neutral. Two sense-fields may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The mind sense-field may be joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The sense-field of mental objects may be joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant, or may not be describable as joined with any of these. Ten sense-fields are neither results nor things that produce results. Two sense-fields may be results, may produce results, or may be neither. ⤵ Five sense-fields are taken up at birth and able to be clung to. The sense-field of sounds is not taken up but able to be clung to. Four sense-fields may be taken up and able to be clung to, or not taken up but able to be clung to. Two sense-fields may be taken up and able to be clung to, not taken up but able to be clung to, or neither taken up nor able to be clung to. Ten sense-fields are undefiled yet open to defilement. Two sense-fields may be defiled and open to defilement, undefiled yet open to defilement, or neither defiled nor open to defilement. Ten sense-fields are without thought and examination. The mind sense-field may have both thought and examination, examination only, or neither. The sense-field of mental objects may have both thought and examination, examination only, or neither, or may not be describable as any of these. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as accompanied by joy, by happiness, or by equanimity. Two sense-fields may be accompanied by joy, by happiness, or by equanimity, or may not be describable as accompanied by any of these. ⤵ Ten sense-fields are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Two sense-fields may be abandoned by seeing, by development, or by neither. Ten sense-fields have root causes to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Two sense-fields may have root causes to be abandoned by seeing, root causes to be abandoned by development, or root causes to be abandoned by neither. Ten sense-fields neither lead to further accumulation nor to dismantling. Two sense-fields may lead to accumulation, to dismantling, or to neither. Ten sense-fields belong neither to trainees nor to those beyond training. Two sense-fields may belong to trainees, to those beyond training, or to neither. Ten sense-fields are limited. Two sense-fields may be limited, expanded, or measureless. Ten sense-fields have no object. Two sense-fields may have a limited object, an expanded object, or a measureless object, or may not be describable as having any of these. Ten sense-fields are middling. Two sense-fields may be inferior, middling, or superior. Ten sense-fields are not fixed in their outcome. Two sense-fields may be fixed in wrongness, fixed in rightness, or not fixed. ⤵ Ten sense-fields have no object. Two sense-fields may have the path as their object, the path as their cause, or the path as their dominant factor, or may not be describable as any of these. Five sense-fields may be arisen or bound to arise; they cannot be described as "not arisen". The sense-field of sounds may be arisen or not arisen; it cannot be described as "bound to arise". Five sense-fields may be arisen, not arisen, or bound to arise. The sense-field of mental objects may be arisen, not arisen, or bound to arise, or may not be describable as any of these. Eleven sense-fields may be past, future, or present. The sense-field of mental objects may be past, future, or present, or may not be describable as past, future, or present. Ten sense-fields have no object. Two sense-fields may have a past object, a future object, or a present object, or may not be describable as having any of these; they may be internal, external, or both internal and external. Ten sense-fields have no object. Two sense-fields may have an internal object, an external object, or an object both internal and external, or may not be describable as having any of these. The sense-field of sights is visible and offers resistance. Nine sense-fields are invisible and offer resistance. Two sense-fields are invisible and offer no resistance.
2. The Pairs

Eleven sense-fields are not root causes. The sense-field of mental objects may be a root cause or not. Ten sense-fields are without root causes. Two sense-fields may have root causes or not. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from root causes. Two sense-fields may be joined with root causes or dissociated from them. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "root causes with root causes" or as "having root causes without being root causes". The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a root cause with root causes"; it may have root causes without being a root cause, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a root cause with root causes, may have root causes without being a root cause, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "root causes joined with root causes" or as "joined with root causes without being root causes". The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a root cause joined with root causes"; it may be joined with root causes without being a root cause, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a root cause joined with root causes, may be joined with root causes without being a root cause, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields are not root causes and are without root causes. The mind sense-field may be not a root cause with root causes, or not a root cause without root causes. The sense-field of mental objects may be not a root cause with root causes, not a root cause without root causes, or not describable as either. ⤵ Eleven sense-fields have conditions. The sense-field of mental objects may have conditions or be without conditions. Eleven sense-fields are compounded. The sense-field of mental objects may be compounded or uncompounded. The sense-field of sights is visible. Eleven sense-fields are invisible. Ten sense-fields offer resistance. Two sense-fields offer no resistance. Ten sense-fields are material. The mind sense-field is immaterial. The sense-field of mental objects may be material or immaterial. Ten sense-fields are worldly. Two sense-fields may be worldly or beyond the world; all are knowable by some kinds of consciousness and not knowable by others. ⤵ Eleven sense-fields are not mental taints. The sense-field of mental objects may be a taint or not. Ten sense-fields are subject to the taints. Two sense-fields may be subject to the taints or free of them. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from the taints. Two sense-fields may be joined with the taints or dissociated from them. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "taints subject to the taints"; they are subject to the taints without being taints. The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a taint subject to the taints"; it may be subject to the taints without being a taint, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a taint subject to the taints, may be subject to the taints without being a taint, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "taints joined with the taints" or as "joined with the taints without being taints". The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a taint joined with the taints"; it may be joined with the taints without being a taint, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a taint joined with the taints, may be joined with the taints without being a taint, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from the taints yet subject to them. Two sense-fields may be dissociated from the taints yet subject to them, dissociated from them and free of them, or not describable as either. ⤵ Eleven sense-fields are not fetters. The sense-field of mental objects may be a fetter or not. Ten sense-fields can be bound by the fetters. Two sense-fields may be able to be bound or not. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from the fetters. Two sense-fields may be joined with the fetters or dissociated from them. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "fetters that can be bound"; they can be bound without being fetters. The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a fetter that can be bound"; it may be able to be bound without being a fetter, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a fetter that can be bound, may be able to be bound without being a fetter, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "fetters joined with the fetters" or as "joined with the fetters without being fetters". The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a fetter joined with the fetters"; it may be joined with the fetters without being a fetter, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a fetter joined with the fetters, may be joined with the fetters without being a fetter, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from the fetters yet able to be bound. Two sense-fields may be dissociated from the fetters yet able to be bound, dissociated from them and unable to be bound, or not describable as either. ⤵ Eleven sense-fields are not ties. The sense-field of mental objects may be a tie or not. Ten sense-fields can be tied. Two sense-fields may be able to be tied or not. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from the ties. Two sense-fields may be joined with the ties or dissociated from them. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "ties that can be tied"; they can be tied without being ties. The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a tie that can be tied"; it may be able to be tied without being a tie, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a tie that can be tied, may be able to be tied without being a tie, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "ties joined with the ties" or as "joined with the ties without being ties". The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a tie joined with the ties"; it may be joined with the ties without being a tie, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a tie joined with the ties, may be joined with the ties without being a tie, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from the ties yet able to be tied. Two sense-fields may be dissociated from the ties yet able to be tied, dissociated from them and unable to be tied, or not describable as either. ⤵ Eleven sense-fields are not floods… not yokes… not hindrances. The sense-field of mental objects may be a hindrance or not. Ten sense-fields can be obstructed by the hindrances. Two sense-fields may be able to be obstructed or not. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from the hindrances. Two sense-fields may be joined with the hindrances or dissociated from them. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "hindrances that can be obstructed"; they can be obstructed without being hindrances. The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a hindrance that can be obstructed"; it may be able to be obstructed without being a hindrance, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a hindrance that can be obstructed, may be able to be obstructed without being a hindrance, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "hindrances joined with the hindrances" or as "joined with the hindrances without being hindrances". The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a hindrance joined with the hindrances"; it may be joined with the hindrances without being a hindrance, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a hindrance joined with the hindrances, may be joined with the hindrances without being a hindrance, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from the hindrances yet able to be obstructed. Two sense-fields may be dissociated from the hindrances yet able to be obstructed, dissociated from them and unable to be obstructed, or not describable as either. ⤵ Eleven sense-fields are not wrong grasping. The sense-field of mental objects may be wrong grasping or not. Ten sense-fields can be wrongly grasped. Two sense-fields may be able to be wrongly grasped or not. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from wrong grasping. The mind sense-field may be joined with wrong grasping or dissociated from it. The sense-field of mental objects may be joined with wrong grasping, dissociated from it, or not describable as either. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "wrong grasping that can be wrongly grasped"; they can be wrongly grasped without being wrong grasping. The mind sense-field cannot be described as "wrong grasping that can be wrongly grasped"; it may be able to be wrongly grasped without being wrong grasping, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be wrong grasping that can be wrongly grasped, may be able to be wrongly grasped without being wrong grasping, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from wrong grasping yet able to be wrongly grasped. Two sense-fields may be dissociated from wrong grasping yet able to be wrongly grasped, dissociated from it and unable to be wrongly grasped, or not describable as either. ⤵ Ten sense-fields have no object. The mind sense-field has an object. The sense-field of mental objects may have an object or no object. The mind sense-field is mind. Eleven sense-fields are not mind. Eleven sense-fields are not mental factors. The sense-field of mental objects may be a mental factor or not. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from mind. The sense-field of mental objects may be joined with mind or dissociated from it. The mind sense-field cannot be described as "joined with mind" or as "dissociated from mind". Ten sense-fields are not mingled with mind. The sense-field of mental objects may be mingled with mind or not. The mind sense-field cannot be described as "mingled with mind" or as "not mingled with mind". Six sense-fields are not produced by mind. Six sense-fields may be produced by mind or not. Eleven sense-fields do not arise together with mind. The sense-field of mental objects may arise together with mind or not. Eleven sense-fields do not follow along with mind. The sense-field of mental objects may follow along with mind or not. Eleven sense-fields are not mingled with mind and produced by it. The sense-field of mental objects may be mingled with mind and produced by it, or not. Eleven sense-fields are not mingled with mind, produced by it, and arising together with it. The sense-field of mental objects may be mingled with mind, produced by it, and arising together with it, or not. Eleven sense-fields are not mingled with mind, produced by it, and following along with it. The sense-field of mental objects may be mingled with mind, produced by it, and following along with it, or not. ⤵ Six sense-fields are internal. Six sense-fields are external. Nine sense-fields are derived. Two sense-fields are not derived. The sense-field of mental objects may be derived or not. Five sense-fields are taken up at birth. The sense-field of sounds is not taken up. Six sense-fields may be taken up or not. Eleven sense-fields are not clinging. The sense-field of mental objects may be clinging or not. Ten sense-fields can be clung to. Two sense-fields may be able to be clung to or not. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from clinging. Two sense-fields may be joined with clinging or dissociated from it. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "clinging that can be clung to"; they can be clung to without being clinging. The mind sense-field cannot be described as "clinging that can be clung to"; it may be able to be clung to without being clinging, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be clinging that can be clung to, may be able to be clung to without being clinging, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "clinging joined with clinging" or as "joined with clinging without being clinging". The mind sense-field cannot be described as "clinging joined with clinging"; it may be joined with clinging without being clinging, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be clinging joined with clinging, may be joined with clinging without being clinging, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from clinging yet able to be clung to. Two sense-fields may be dissociated from clinging yet able to be clung to, dissociated from it and unable to be clung to, or not describable as either. ⤵ Eleven sense-fields are not defilements. The sense-field of mental objects may be a defilement or not. Ten sense-fields are open to defilement. Two sense-fields may be open to defilement or not. Ten sense-fields are undefiled. Two sense-fields may be defiled or undefiled. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from the defilements. Two sense-fields may be joined with the defilements or dissociated from them. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "defilements open to defilement"; they are open to defilement without being defilements. The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a defilement open to defilement"; it may be open to defilement without being a defilement, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a defilement open to defilement, may be open to defilement without being a defilement, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "defilements that are defiled" or as "defiled without being defilements". The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a defilement that is defiled"; it may be defiled without being a defilement, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a defilement that is defiled, may be defiled without being a defilement, or may not be describable as either. ⤵ Ten sense-fields cannot be described as "defilements joined with the defilements" or as "joined with the defilements without being defilements". The mind sense-field cannot be described as "a defilement joined with the defilements"; it may be joined with the defilements without being a defilement, or may not be describable as such. The sense-field of mental objects may be a defilement joined with the defilements, may be joined with the defilements without being a defilement, or may not be describable as either. Ten sense-fields are dissociated from the defilements yet open to defilement. Two sense-fields may be dissociated from the defilements yet open to defilement, dissociated from them and not open to defilement, or not describable as either. ⤵ Ten sense-fields are not to be abandoned by seeing. Two sense-fields may be abandoned by seeing or not. Ten sense-fields are not to be abandoned by meditative development. Two sense-fields may be abandoned by development or not. Ten sense-fields do not have root causes to be abandoned by seeing. Two sense-fields may have root causes to be abandoned by seeing or not. Ten sense-fields do not have root causes to be abandoned by development. Two sense-fields may have root causes to be abandoned by development or not. Ten sense-fields are without thought. Two sense-fields may have thought or not. Ten sense-fields are without examination. Two sense-fields may have examination or not. Ten sense-fields are without joy. Two sense-fields may have joy or not. Ten sense-fields are not accompanied by joy. Two sense-fields may be accompanied by joy or not. Ten sense-fields are not accompanied by happiness. Two sense-fields may be accompanied by happiness or not. Ten sense-fields are not accompanied by equanimity. Two sense-fields may be accompanied by equanimity or not. ⤵ Ten sense-fields belong to the sense sphere. Two sense-fields may belong to the sense sphere or not. Ten sense-fields do not belong to the fine-material sphere. Two sense-fields may belong to the fine-material sphere or not. Ten sense-fields do not belong to the immaterial sphere. Two sense-fields may belong to the immaterial sphere or not. Ten sense-fields are included in the round of existence. Two sense-fields may be included in the round of existence or outside it. Ten sense-fields do not lead out of the round. Two sense-fields may lead out of the round or not. Ten sense-fields are not fixed in their outcome. Two sense-fields may be fixed or not fixed. Ten sense-fields can be surpassed. Two sense-fields may be surpassable or unsurpassable. Ten sense-fields are free from conflict. Two sense-fields may involve conflict or be free from conflict.
The Section of Questions and Answers is finished.
The Analysis of the Sense-Fields is finished.
3. Analysis of the Elements
1. Classification According to the Discourses
There are six elements – the earth element, the water element, the fire element, the air element, the space element, and the consciousness element.

Therein, what is the earth element? The earth element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal earth element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is hard, solid, hardness, the state of being hard, internal and taken up at birth – namely: head hair, body hair, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, membranes, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, stomach contents, and excrement; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is hard, solid, hardness, the state of being hard, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal earth element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external earth element? Whatever externally is hard, solid, hardness, the state of being hard, external and not taken up – namely: iron, copper, tin, lead, silver ore, pearl, gems, cat's-eye, conch shell, stone, coral, silver, gold, ruby, emerald, grass, wood, gravel, potsherds, earth, rock, and mountains; or whatever else externally is hard, solid, hardness, the state of being hard, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external earth element'. The internal earth element and the external earth element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the earth element".

Therein, what is the water element? The water element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal water element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is water, watery, moisture, moistness, the cohesion of material form, internal and taken up at birth – namely: bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, mucus, joint fluid, and urine; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is water, watery, moisture, moistness, the cohesion of material form, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal water element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external water element? Whatever externally is water, watery, moisture, moistness, the cohesion of material form, external and not taken up – namely: the juice of roots, the juice of stems, the juice of bark, the juice of leaves, the juice of flowers, the juice of fruits, milk, curds, ghee, butter, oil, honey, molasses, and the waters of the earth or of the sky; or whatever else externally is water, watery, moisture, moistness, the cohesion of material form, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external water element'. The internal water element and the external water element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the water element".

Therein, what is the fire element? The fire element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal fire element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is fire, fiery, heat, heatedness, warmth, warmness, internal and taken up at birth – namely: that by which one is warmed, that by which one ages, that by which one is burned, and that by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted is fully digested; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is fire, fiery, heat, heatedness, warmth, warmness, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal fire element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external fire element? Whatever externally is fire, fiery, heat, heatedness, warmth, warmness, external and not taken up – namely: fire of wood, fire of straw, fire of grass, fire of cow dung, fire of husks, fire of rubbish, lightning fire, the heat of fire, the heat of the sun, the heat of a heap of wood, the heat of a heap of grass, the heat of a heap of grain, the heat of a heap of goods; or whatever else externally is fire, fiery, heat, heatedness, warmth, warmness, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external fire element'. The internal fire element and the external fire element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the fire element".

Therein, what is the air element? The air element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal air element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is air, airy, the distension of material form, internal and taken up at birth – namely: winds going upward, winds going downward, winds in the belly, winds in the bowels, winds coursing through the limbs, cutting winds, piercing winds, throbbing winds, breathing in and breathing out; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is air, airy, the distension of material form, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal air element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external air element? Whatever externally is air, airy, the distension of material form, external and not taken up – namely: east winds, west winds, north winds, south winds, dusty winds, dust-free winds, cold winds, hot winds, gentle winds, strong winds, black winds, high-altitude winds, winds from birds' wings, winds from a supaṇṇa bird, winds from palm-leaf fans, winds from a winnowing fan; or whatever else externally is air, airy, the distension of material form, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external air element'. The internal air element and the external air element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the air element".

Therein, what is the space element? The space element is twofold: there is internal and there is external. Therein, what is the internal space element? Whatever internally, in oneself, is space, spatial, a void, a hollow, an opening, a gap, not touched by flesh and blood, internal and taken up at birth – namely: the opening of the ear, the opening of the nose, the door of the mouth, that by which one swallows what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted, that in which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted stays, and that by which what is eaten, drunk, chewed, and tasted passes out below; or whatever else internally, in oneself, is space, spatial, a void, a hollow, an opening, a gap, not touched by flesh and blood, internal and taken up at birth – this is called 'the internal space element'. ⤵ Therein, what is the external space element? Whatever externally is space, spatial, a void, a hollow, an opening, a gap, not touched by the four great elements, external and not taken up – this is called 'the external space element'. The internal space element and the external space element, gathered and grouped together: this is called "the space element".

Therein, what is the consciousness element? The eye-consciousness element, the ear-consciousness element, the nose-consciousness element, the tongue-consciousness element, the body-consciousness element, and the mind-consciousness element – this is called "the consciousness element".
These are the six elements.
There are another six elements – the pleasure element, the pain element, the gladness element, the sadness element, the equanimity element, and the ignorance element.

Therein, what is the pleasure element? Bodily comfort, bodily pleasure; the comfortable, pleasant experience born of body-contact; the comfortable, pleasant feeling born of body-contact – this is called "the pleasure element". ⤵ Therein, what is the pain element? Bodily discomfort, bodily pain; the uncomfortable, painful experience born of body-contact; the uncomfortable, painful feeling born of body-contact – this is called "the pain element". ⤵ Therein, what is the gladness element? Mental comfort, mental pleasure; the comfortable, pleasant experience born of mind-contact; the comfortable, pleasant feeling born of mind-contact – this is called "the gladness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the sadness element? Mental discomfort, mental pain; the uncomfortable, painful experience born of mind-contact; the uncomfortable, painful feeling born of mind-contact – this is called "the sadness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the equanimity element? What is mentally neither comfortable nor uncomfortable; the experience born of mind-contact that is neither painful nor pleasant; the feeling born of mind-contact that is neither painful nor pleasant – this is called "the equanimity element". ⤵ Therein, what is the ignorance element? Not knowing, not seeing, not comprehending, not awakening, not fully awakening, not penetrating, not grasping, not fathoming, not weighing evenly, not reflecting, not seeing directly; poor discernment, foolishness, lack of clear understanding; delusion, bewilderment, complete confusion; ignorance, the flood of ignorance, the yoke of ignorance, the underlying tendency to ignorance, the obsession of ignorance, the barrier of ignorance; delusion, the root of the unwholesome – this is called "the ignorance element".
These are the six elements.
There are another six elements – the element of sense desire, the element of ill will, the element of cruelty, the element of renunciation, the element of goodwill, and the element of harmlessness.

Therein, what is the element of sense desire? Thinking connected with sense desire – thought, intention, fixing, focusing, directing the mind, wrong intention – this is called the element of sense desire. Taking the Avīci hell as the lower limit and the gods who wield power over others' creations as the upper limit, whatever within this range moves here and is included here – the aggregates, elements, and sense-fields, material form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness – this is called "the element of sense desire". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of ill will? Thinking connected with ill will – thought… wrong intention – this is called "the element of ill will". Or the mind's irritation over the ten grounds for resentment: hostility, resistance, opposition; anger, rage, fury; hatred, ill feeling, malice; the mind's vexation, mental resentment; anger, being angry, the state of being angry; hatred, hating, the state of hating; vexation, being vexed; opposition, hostility; ferocity, harshness, and the mind's displeasure – this is called "the element of ill will". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of cruelty? Thinking connected with cruelty – thought… wrong intention – this is called "the element of cruelty". Here someone harms living beings with a hand, a clod, a stick, a knife, a rope, or with one thing or another; such tormenting, harassing, hurting, injuring, provoking, and attacking of others – this is called "the element of cruelty". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of renunciation? Thinking connected with renunciation – thought… right intention – this is called "the element of renunciation". Indeed, all wholesome states are "the element of renunciation". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of goodwill? Thinking connected with goodwill – thought… right intention – this is called "the element of goodwill". Loving-kindness towards living beings, the act of loving, the state of loving, the liberation of mind through loving-kindness – this is called "the element of goodwill". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of harmlessness? Thinking connected with harmlessness – thought, intention, fixing, focusing, directing the mind, right intention – this is called "the element of harmlessness". Compassion towards living beings, the act of compassion, the state of compassion, the liberation of mind through compassion – this is called "the element of harmlessness".
These are the six elements.
Thus these three sets of six, gathered and grouped together, make eighteen elements.
The Classification According to the Discourses is finished.
2. Classification According to the Abhidhamma

There are eighteen elements – the eye element, the element of sights, the eye-consciousness element; the ear element, the element of sounds, the ear-consciousness element; the nose element, the element of smells, the nose-consciousness element; the tongue element, the element of tastes, the tongue-consciousness element; the body element, the element of things touched, the body-consciousness element; the mind element, the element of mental objects, and the mind-consciousness element.

Therein, what is the eye element? The eye that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements… this is an empty village – this is called "the eye element". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of sights? The sight that is the shining of colour derived from the four great elements… this is the element of sights – this is called "the element of sights". ⤵ Therein, what is the eye-consciousness element? Depending on the eye and sights there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding eye-consciousness element – this is called "the eye-consciousness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the ear element? The ear that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements… this is an empty village – this is called "the ear element". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of sounds? The sound that is derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance… this is the element of sounds – this is called "the element of sounds". ⤵ Therein, what is the ear-consciousness element? Depending on the ear and sounds there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding ear-consciousness element – this is called "the ear-consciousness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the nose element? The nose that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements… this is an empty village – this is called "the nose element". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of smells? The smell that is derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance… this is the element of smells – this is called "the element of smells". ⤵ Therein, what is the nose-consciousness element? Depending on the nose and smells there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding nose-consciousness element – this is called "the nose-consciousness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the tongue element? The tongue that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements… this is an empty village – this is called "the tongue element". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of tastes? The taste that is derived from the four great elements, invisible and offering resistance… this is the element of tastes – this is called "the element of tastes". ⤵ Therein, what is the tongue-consciousness element? Depending on the tongue and tastes there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding tongue-consciousness element – this is called "the tongue-consciousness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the body element? The body that is a sensitive surface derived from the four great elements… this is an empty village – this is called "the body element". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of things touched? The earth element… this is the element of things touched – this is called "the element of things touched". ⤵ Therein, what is the body-consciousness element? Depending on the body and things touched there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding body-consciousness element – this is called "the body-consciousness element". ⤵ Therein, what is the mind element? Immediately after the arising and ceasing of the eye-consciousness element there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding mind element; immediately after the arising and ceasing of the ear-consciousness element… of the nose-consciousness element… of the tongue-consciousness element… of the body-consciousness element there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding mind element; or, at the first turning of attention towards any object whatever there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding mind element – this is called "the mind element". ⤵ Therein, what is the element of mental objects? The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, the material form that is invisible and offers no resistance and is included in the sense-field of mental objects, and the unconditioned element. ⤵ Therein, what is the aggregate of feeling? As a single class, the aggregate of feeling is joined with contact. As a twofold class: there is feeling with a root cause, and feeling without one. As a threefold class: there is wholesome feeling, unwholesome feeling, and neutral feeling… thus the aggregate of feeling is classified up to ten ways… thus the aggregate of feeling is classified in many ways. This is called "the aggregate of feeling". ⤵ Therein, what is the aggregate of perception? As a single class, the aggregate of perception is joined with contact. As a twofold class: there is perception with a root cause, and perception without one. As a threefold class: there is wholesome perception, unwholesome perception, and neutral perception… thus the aggregate of perception is classified up to ten ways… thus the aggregate of perception is classified in many ways. This is called "the aggregate of perception". ⤵ Therein, what is the aggregate of mental formations? As a single class, the aggregate of mental formations is joined with mind. As a twofold class: there are formations that are root causes, and formations that are not. As a threefold class: there are wholesome formations, unwholesome formations, and neutral formations… thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified up to ten ways… thus the aggregate of mental formations is classified in many ways. This is called "the aggregate of mental formations". ⤵ Therein, what is the material form that is invisible, offers no resistance, and is included in the sense-field of mental objects? The faculty of femininity… physical food – this is called the material form that is "invisible, offers no resistance, and is included in the sense-field of mental objects". ⤵ Therein, what is the unconditioned element? The ending of desire, the ending of hatred, and the ending of delusion – this is called "the unconditioned element". This is called "the element of mental objects". ⤵ Therein, what is the mind-consciousness element? Immediately after the arising and ceasing of the eye-consciousness element there arises the mind element, and immediately after the arising and ceasing of the mind element there arises mind, mentality, mental activity… and the corresponding mind-consciousness element; immediately after the arising and ceasing of the ear-consciousness element… of the nose-consciousness element… of the tongue-consciousness element… of the body-consciousness element there arises the mind element, and immediately after the arising and ceasing of that mind element there arises mind, mentality, mental activity… and the corresponding mind-consciousness element; and depending on the mind and mental objects there arises mind, mentality, mental activity, heart, the bright one, mind, the mind sense-field, the mind faculty, consciousness, the aggregate of consciousness, and the corresponding mind-consciousness element – this is called "the mind-consciousness element".
The Classification According to the Abhidhamma is finished.
3. The Section of Questions and Answers

There are eighteen elements – the eye element, the element of sights, the eye-consciousness element; the ear element, the element of sounds, the ear-consciousness element; the nose element, the element of smells, the nose-consciousness element; the tongue element, the element of tastes, the tongue-consciousness element; the body element, the element of things touched, the body-consciousness element; the mind element, the element of mental objects, and the mind-consciousness element.
Of the eighteen elements, how many are wholesome, how many unwholesome, how many neutral… how many involve conflict, how many are free from conflict?
1. The Triads

Sixteen elements are neutral. Two elements may be wholesome, unwholesome, or neutral. Ten elements cannot be described as joined with pleasant feeling, joined with painful feeling, or joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. Five elements are joined with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The body-consciousness element may be joined with pleasant feeling or with painful feeling. The mind-consciousness element may be joined with pleasant feeling, with painful feeling, or with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant. The element of mental objects may be joined with pleasant feeling, with painful feeling, or with feeling that is neither painful nor pleasant, or may not be describable as joined with any of these. ⤵ Ten elements are neither results nor things that produce results. Five elements are results. The mind element may be a result, or neither a result nor something that produces results. Two elements may be results, may produce results, or may be neither. ⤵ Ten elements are taken up at birth and able to be clung to. The element of sounds is not taken up but able to be clung to. Five elements may be taken up and able to be clung to, or not taken up but able to be clung to. Two elements may be taken up and able to be clung to, not taken up but able to be clung to, or neither taken up nor able to be clung to. ⤵ Sixteen elements are undefiled yet open to defilement. Two elements may be defiled and open to defilement, undefiled yet open to defilement, or neither defiled nor open to defilement. Fifteen elements are without thought and examination. The mind element has both thought and examination. The mind-consciousness element may have both thought and examination, examination only, or neither. The element of mental objects may have both thought and examination, examination only, or neither, or may not be describable as any of these. Ten elements cannot be described as accompanied by joy, by happiness, or by equanimity. Five elements are accompanied by equanimity. The body-consciousness element is not accompanied by joy; it may be accompanied by happiness or not; it is not accompanied by equanimity; or it may not be describable as "accompanied by happiness". Two elements may be accompanied by joy, by happiness, or by equanimity, or may not be describable as accompanied by any of these. ⤵ Sixteen elements are to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by meditative development. Two elements may be abandoned by seeing, by development, or by neither. Sixteen elements have root causes to be abandoned neither by seeing nor by development. Two elements may have root causes to be abandoned by seeing, root causes to be abandoned by development, or root causes to be abandoned by neither. Sixteen elements neither lead to further accumulation nor to dismantling. Two elements may lead to accumulation, to dismantling, or to neither. Sixteen elements belong neither to trainees nor to those beyond training. Two elements may belong to trainees, to those beyond training, or to neither. ⤵ Sixteen elements are limited. Two elements may be limited, expanded, or measureless. Ten elements have no object. Six elements have a limited object. Two elements may have a limited object, an expanded object, or a measureless object, or may not be describable as having any of these. Sixteen elements are middling. Two elements may be inferior, middling, or superior. Sixteen elements are not fixed in their outcome. Two elements may be fixed in wrongness, fixed in rightness, or not fixed. ⤵ Ten elements have no object. Six elements cannot be described as having the path as their object, the path as their cause, or the path as their dominant factor. Two elements may have the path as their object, the path as their cause, or the path as their dominant factor, or may not be describable as any of these. Ten elements may be arisen or bound to arise; they cannot be described as "not arisen". The element of sounds may be arisen or not arisen; it cannot be described as "bound to arise". Six elements may be arisen, not arisen, or bound to arise. 4. Analysis of the Truths
1. Classification According to the Discourses

There are four noble truths – the noble truth of suffering, the noble truth of the origin of suffering, the noble truth of the ending of suffering, and the noble truth of the way leading to the ending of suffering.
1. The Truth of Suffering

Therein, what is the noble truth of suffering? Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, death is suffering; sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and despair are suffering; association with what is disliked is suffering; separation from what is loved is suffering; not getting what one wants is also suffering; in brief, the five aggregates that are clung to are suffering.

Therein, what is birth? The birth of this or that being into this or that order of beings – the being born, the descent, the coming forth, the appearance of the aggregates, the acquiring of the sense-fields – this is called "birth".

Therein, what is aging? The aging of this or that being in this or that order of beings – the growing old, brokenness of teeth, greyness of hair, wrinkling of skin, the decline of the life span, the ripening of the faculties – this is called "aging".

Therein, what is death? The passing of this or that being from this or that order of beings – the passing away, the breaking up, the disappearance, mortality, death, the completion of one's time, the breaking up of the aggregates, the laying down of the body, the cutting off of the life faculty – this is called "death".

Therein, what is sorrow? When someone is touched by loss of relatives, loss of wealth, loss through illness, loss of virtue, or loss of view, when someone meets with one misfortune or another, is touched by one painful thing or another – the sorrow, the sorrowing, the state of sorrow, inner sorrow, deep inner sorrow, the burning of the mind, sadness, the dart of sorrow – this is called "sorrow".

Therein, what is lamentation? When someone is touched by loss of relatives, loss of wealth, loss through illness, loss of virtue, or loss of view, when someone meets with one misfortune or another, is touched by one painful thing or another – the crying out, the lamenting, the act of crying out, the act of lamenting, the state of crying out, the state of lamenting; the talk, the raving, the wailing; the moaning, the act of moaning, the state of moaning – this is called "lamentation".
Therein, what is pain? Bodily discomfort, bodily pain; the uncomfortable, painful experience born of body-contact; the uncomfortable, painful feeling born of body-contact – this is called "pain".

Therein, what is sadness? Mental discomfort, mental pain; the uncomfortable, painful experience born of mind-contact; the uncomfortable, painful feeling born of mind-contact – this is called "sadness".

Therein, what is despair? When someone is touched by loss of relatives, loss of wealth, loss through illness, loss of virtue, or loss of view, when someone meets with one misfortune or another, is touched by one painful thing or another – the distress, the despair, the state of distress, the state of despair – this is called "despair".

Therein, what is the suffering of association with what is disliked? Here, whatever sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and things touched are unwanted, unattractive, and disagreeable to someone, or whoever wishes them ill, wishes them harm, wishes them discomfort, wishes them no security – meeting, coming together, joining, and mingling with these – this is called "the suffering of association with what is disliked".

Therein, what is the suffering of separation from what is loved? Here, whatever sights, sounds, smells, tastes, and things touched are wanted, attractive, and agreeable to someone, or whoever wishes them well, wishes them good, wishes them comfort, wishes them security – mother or father, brother or sister, friends or companions, relatives or kin – not meeting, not coming together, not joining, and not mingling with these – this is called "the suffering of separation from what is loved".

Therein, what is "not getting what one wants is also suffering"? In beings subject to birth such a wish arises: "Oh, that we were not subject to birth! Oh, that birth would not come to us!" But this cannot be gained by wishing. This too is "not getting what one wants is also suffering". ⤵ In beings subject to aging… in beings subject to illness… in beings subject to death… in beings subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and despair such a wish arises: "Oh, that we were not subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and despair! Oh, that sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and despair would not come to us!" But this cannot be gained by wishing. This too is "not getting what one wants is also suffering".

Therein, what is "in brief, the five aggregates that are clung to are suffering"? Namely: the aggregate of material form that is clung to, the aggregate of feeling that is clung to, the aggregate of perception that is clung to, the aggregate of mental formations that is clung to, and the aggregate of consciousness that is clung to. These are called "in brief, the five aggregates that are clung to are suffering". ⤵ This is called "the noble truth of suffering".

4. The Truth of the Path

Therein, what is the noble truth of the way leading to the ending of suffering? It is just this noble eightfold path, namely: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration. ⤵ Therein, what is right view? Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the ending of suffering, knowledge of the way leading to the ending of suffering – this is called "right view". ⤵ Therein, what is right intention? The intention of renunciation, the intention of goodwill, the intention of harmlessness – this is called "right intention". ⤵ Therein, what is right speech? Refraining from false speech, refraining from divisive speech, refraining from harsh speech, refraining from idle chatter – this is called "right speech". ⤵ Therein, what is right action? Refraining from killing living beings, refraining from taking what is not given, refraining from sexual misconduct – this is called "right action". ⤵ Therein, what is right livelihood? Here a noble disciple, having abandoned wrong livelihood, makes a living by right livelihood – this is called "right livelihood". ⤵ Therein, what is right effort? Here a monk generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies the mind, and endeavours for the non-arising of bad, unwholesome states that have not yet arisen. He generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies the mind, and endeavours for the abandoning of bad, unwholesome states that have arisen. He generates desire, strives, arouses energy, applies the mind, and endeavours for the arising of wholesome states that have not yet arisen.
